messages:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - MULTI-REGION FAILOVER ALERT: MR-2026-0605-07. Detected abnormal routing between us-west-1 and eu-central-1 causing failed cross-region traffic shifts for hosted endpoints. Paging on-call.

olivia: oncall here, ack. Seeing 502/504 spikes for customers routed to eu-central-1; at same time some requests still go to us-west-1 where ALBs report high target-group unhealthy. Starting bridge.

paul: neteng - provider reports maintenance splice in us-west fiber cluster causing intermittent path asymmetry and packet drops. BGP sessions stable but partial prefixes are announced via suboptimal path causing blackholing from some ISP peers.

quinn: eng-sre - automated failover tried to move traffic to eu-central but DNS TTL was set to 300s for a subset of records due to a historical override by a legacy infra job (ugh). That prevented rapid client switchover.

olivia: customer impact quick: ~20% increased 5xx, a few premium customers reporting request id clusters failing; some SDKs aggressively retrying causing amplified load. CS has inbound.

rita: infra-eng - confirmed ALB stickiness (cookie-based) is keeping long-lived clients hitting us-west despite DNS change. Also conntrack tables on edge NAT boxes are holding state; even if DNS changes, TCP sessions persist.

paul: mitigation plan: 1) reduce Route53 TTL to 15s for affected records, 2) apply manual BGP community to prefer eu-central announcements from our peering fabric, 3) decrease ALB stickiness and deregistration delay to 20s, 4) prewarm eu-central model pools and enable lightweight fallback model.

quinn: running TTL patch now. Script:

```
# Reduce TTL for emergency failover
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZEU12345 --change-batch '{
  "Changes":[{
    "Action":"UPSERT",
    "ResourceRecordSet":{
      "Name":"api.redwood.com",
      "Type":"A",
      "TTL":15,
      "ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"93.184.216.34"}]
    }
  }]}
'
```

rita: applying ALB: setting stickiness off on affected target groups and lowering deregistration delay to 20s. Also clearing conntrack entries on edge NATs to drop stale sessions.

paul: contacting our peering ops to push BGP community change to prefer EU path. This will shift transit-level preference quicker than DNS in some cases.

infra-eng: peering ops confirmed they added community no-export override; should see route preference in ~2 minutes. Watching route table.

olivia: starting pre-warm in eu-central: spinning +80% model workers and preloading hot shards; enabling quantized fallback for new sessions at 10% canary.

ops-cs: crafting customer note: "We are aware of increased errors affecting some requests. Engineers are shifting traffic and scaling capacity. If you see repeated failures, please provide request IDs; we are prioritizing dedicated tenants." Approve?

olivia: approve. Add note to suggest client-side retry backoff to avoid duplicate charges.

quinn: metrics update: after TTL change and BGP adjustment, route preference to eu-central increased to ~70% within 2 minutes. But we see a spike of 503s in eu-central due to cold model pools for initial shifted traffic.

rita: the cold-start 503s are real. Increasing warm workers and enabling fallback quant-model more widely to 50% now. Also pre-populating Redis hotkeys.

paul: also noticed some enterprise customers behind old corporate proxies that map DNS name to hardcoded IPs via hosts files. We should notify account teams to ping those customers.

ops-cs: flagged two enterprise accounts (AC-77, BIZ-9) for outreach. AEs notified.

olivia: canary results: quantized fallback at 10% reduced 503s in canary to near zero. Rolling to 50% cut 503s across shifted traffic by ~65%. Tail latency still elevated but trending down.

infra-eng: ALB stickiness change and conntrack clear helped reduce persistent traffic to us-west. us-west target groups still show high unhealthy counts due to backend connection resets; investigating cleanup tasks there.

paul: peering partner reports that their caches respected new communities and we see full preference flip in their peering fabric. However residual traffic remains because of DNS caches and hosts overrides.

quinn: to avoid flip-flop we are NOT going to oscillate weights. Plan: hold at eu-central preference while we stabilize, then gradually shift any remaining capacity back to us-west if/when healthy.

olivia: customer update sent at 00:40 UTC. Incident bridge open. I'll hand off monitoring to oncall-cover after mitigation.

oncall-cover: ack takeover for 4h watch. Will post status every 30m and page if 5xx > 3% sustained.

rita: final mitigation checklist (completed):
- Route53 TTL lowered to 15s for affected records
- BGP community applied to prefer eu-central announcements
- ALB stickiness disabled; deregistration delay = 20s
- conntrack cleared on edge NATs
- eu-central model pool scaled +80% and hot-shards preloaded
- quantized fallback rolled from 10% -> 50% -> 100% for new sessions
- customer notifications sent and AEs alerted for dedicated tenants

paul: monitoring: within 25 minutes global 5xx rate dropped to baseline +1.5%, tail latency decreasing. No further route withdraws observed.

olivia: marking incident as mitigated in tracker. Creating postmortem ticket PM-2026-0605 with assigned owners: neteng (paul) for peering fix, infra (rita) for cold-start mitigation improvements, devex (quinn) to remove legacy TTL overrides from infra jobs.

ops-cs: follow-up: schedule 1:1 calls with AC-77 and BIZ-9. Provide request IDs and explanation.

quinn: runbook action items (adding to ticket):
1) automate emergency TTL drop when health-checks flapping
2) add pre-warm webhook to scale secondary region on health degradation
3) implement model fallback auto-enable during DNS-based failovers
4) scan repo for legacy TTL overrides and remove

olivia: closing bridge at 01:00 UTC but monitoring continues. If anything new, page oncall.

sre-bot: Incident MR-2026-0605-07 status updated: MITIGATED by olivia at 01:00 UTC. Postmortem scheduled."
